summary: Clade-level tests are possible now: Dryad holds CC0 3D-landmark ontogenetic series for 10 crocodylian species built precisely to compare ontogenetic and phylogenetic transformations (10.5061/dryad.14fn1), plus smaller sets for macaque skulls, mammal forelimbs, dinosaur endocasts and cetacean ear bones, and Open Tree supplies the phylogeny. The claim's universal scope ('one road' across organic form) is far broader than these few vertebrate clades, and MorphoSource juvenile scans are mostly download-restricted, so status is partial rather than data-ready.
next_step: Pre-register a trajectory-angle comparison in the crocodylian dataset (ontogenetic vectors vs. the phylogenetic path on the Open Tree induced subtree), then replicate on the macaque and cetacean sets to see whether the result generalises.
obstacles_confirmed: Most scans are adults, so ontogenetic series have to be assembled clade by clade.
Coverage is strong for a few vertebrate groups and weak for the stated scope of organic form.
